slides.h: I read this aloud twice today. The main claim in both readings is overturned.
b: Recording the correction rather than quietly editing the file — the wrong version is what you heard.
One review, one counterexample, one line long.

slides.h: There is a setting where the model produces no signal at all
b: Two effects cancel each other exactly, so an observer could sit as far off centre as they like and the sky would still look perfectly uniform.
I called it the single most important finding of the phase.

slides.h: Two calculations, incompatible assumptions, the same cancellation
b: If the silence turns up either way, surely it belongs to the model and not to the assumptions.
That was the whole of my reasoning.

slides.h: Same temperature everywhere along the visible boundary
b: Then one of the two effects simply does not exist.
There is nothing for the other one to cancel against, and the signal never vanishes at any setting at all.

slides.h: Two guesses agreeing is a property they share, not a property of the truth
b: The silence belongs to the two descriptions of the material, not to the model.
I treated agreement between guesses as evidence about the thing they were both approximating.

slides.h: The shape is not safe either: about 50 percent, and a change of sign
b: I had said opacity changes only how bright the patch is, not its shape.
I measured it as a percent change in a ratio sitting very close to one — which hides exactly the thing being diagnosed.

slides.h: Not established — and not establishable from the papers
b: Under the two descriptions we could test, the model goes quiet at a particular setting.
Whether the model itself has any silent setting cannot be answered: the papers never say what the material beyond the wall is, or how its heat behaves.
Nothing reaches us from beyond the wall — the boundary's own glow is the only thing that could ever be seen.
How light behaves crossing the boundary: the photon's path drops out entirely, because inside a black hole the radial direction plays the role of time.
A clean analytic law for the motion of the two fluids at the boundary, unchanged since it was first derived.

slides.h: Not with what the papers provide
b: The interior is exactly ordinary, so the usual measurements are blind to it.
Every attempt to compute the one possible signature has meant inventing a description of the material — and the answer changed with each invention.

slides.h: Not that the test is hard — the theory does not contain enough physics to say what the test would show
b: I would rather say the weaker true thing three times over than leave the stronger one standing.
